source_caption:
📺 Switched at Birth (2011–2017)

Switched at Birth follows Bay Kennish and Daphne Vasquez, two teenage girls whose lives change forever when they discover that they were accidentally switched at birth and raised by completely different families. Bay grew up in a wealthy household with loving parents, while Daphne, who lost her hearing as a young child, was raised by her hardworking single mother in a modest neighborhood. After the shocking discovery, both families become deeply involved in each other’s lives, leading to complicated relationships, emotional conflicts, and unexpected challenges. As Bay and Daphne navigate friendships, romantic relationships, school struggles, and questions about their identities, they must also adjust to the differences between their families and backgrounds. Through misunderstandings, personal sacrifices, and life-changing experiences, the girls learn valuable lessons about acceptance, communication, and belonging. Combining heartfelt storytelling, emotional drama, and meaningful family moments, the series explores identity, deaf culture, family relationships, social class, love, and the importance of understanding others.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Family • Romance • Teen Drama

⭐ IMDb: 7.7/10

⏱️ Runtime: ~42 minutes per episode • 5 seasons • 103 episodes

🎥 Creator: Lizzy Weiss

🏆 Recognition: Starring Vanessa Marano, Katie Leclerc, Constance Marie, Lea Thompson, D.W. Moffett, and Marlee Matlin, the series received recognition for its groundbreaking representation of deaf characters and American Sign Language. It earned a Peabody Award and became known for its emotional storytelling, diverse perspectives, and thoughtful exploration of communication, identity, and family.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Hulu, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, and Apple TV for current streaming or digital purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Switched at Birth is an American teen and family drama television series that premiered on ABC Family on June 6, 2011. The one-hour scripted drama is set in the Kansas City metropolitan area, and revolves around two teenagers who were switched at birth and grew up in very different environments: one in an affluent suburb, and the other in a working-class neighborhood. According to ABC Family, it is "the first mainstream television series to have multiple deaf and hard-of-hearing series regulars and scenes shot entirely in American Sign Language (ASL)".
